reason: The 2.51% measures selected native branch cost, not a ranking statistic. Source and evidence archive remain unchanged.

request.body:
All twelve common-root planning slots passed independent native replay. The longer horizon lowered average native branch cost by 7.33%, but was nonworse on only seven of twelve slots against a required eight. Correct-gain scoring lowered selected native branch cost by 2.51%, below the fixed 3% margin. More short search offered no average benefit. All three contrasts failed their continuation rules; this tracking configuration is closed as evidence for learned adaptation.

[Results, chart and limitations](https://github.com/kw2828/OpenJev/blob/main/research/reacher-common-root-diagnostic.md).

The protocol, source and paired inputs were published before execution at `c9a428ad9341db2aa74fe71f8fb6c3c8cc16f00f`. The archive includes all twelve raw slots, complete noisy native branches, candidate searches, cross-scoring, input arrays, source snapshots, native audits, reviews and the source episode records used to extract roots. Every archive member was reopened and hashed against `members.json`.

Execution took 7.324 seconds and replay 13.034 seconds, covering 413,928 transitions each. This is an open-loop diagnostic on exposed engineering histories with ten distinct native states, not a closed-loop benchmark, learned model, deployment speedup or architectural result. No weights are included. Original path bindings and runtime assumptions are preserved.
